paragraphs: God, Exalted, has among His servants chosen ones whom He selects and singles out, and upon whom He bestows lofty virtues, sublime qualities, beneficial knowledge, righteous deeds and distinctions of many kinds. So He mentioned these great households and the perfect men they contained, men who attained the attributes of perfection, and that excellence and goodness ran on in succession through their offspring, embracing both their males and their females. This is among the greatest of His favours and the finest of the places where His generosity and bounty alight. And God is Hearing, Knowing (3:34): He knows who deserves favour and preferment, and so He places His favour where His wisdom requires.

When He had established the greatness of these households, He mentioned the story of Mary and her son Jesus (peace and blessings be upon him): how the two of them descended from these excellent households, how their circumstances passed from one state to another from the beginning of their affair to its end, and how the wife of ʿImrān said, imploring her Lord and drawing near to Him by this act of devotion which He loves, an act which contains the veneration of His House and constant attendance upon His obedience: I have vowed to You what is in my womb, consecrated, that is, as a servant of the house of worship that was thronged with worshippers; so accept it from me, that is, this deed: make it founded upon faith and sincerity and fruitful in goodness and reward; indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing (3:35).

Then when she delivered her, she said: My Lord, I have delivered a female, and God knew best what she delivered, and the male is not like the female (3:36). It is as though in these words there is a kind of imploring on her part and a brokenness of spirit, since her vow had been made on the basis that the child would be a male, from whom would come the strength, the service and the discharge of that duty which come from people of strength, whereas a female is otherwise.

So God mended her heart and God accepted her vow, and this female became more complete and more perfect than many males, indeed than most of them, and through her were achieved purposes greater than those achieved through a male. For this reason He said: So her Lord accepted her with a goodly acceptance and made her grow with a goodly growth, that is, she was reared with a wonderful upbringing, religious, moral and refined, by which her circumstances were perfected, her words and deeds were made sound, and her perfection grew within her. God made Zachariah easy for her as a guardian, and it is one of God's favours upon a servant that He appoints as the one who undertakes his upbringing someone from among the perfect and the righteous.

Then God, Exalted, honoured Mary and Zachariah, in that He made easy for Mary provision that came without toil or weariness; it was rather a miraculous favour (karāma) with which God honoured her, since whenever Zachariah entered upon her in the sanctuary, which is the place of worship (in which there is an indication of the abundance of her prayer and her constant attendance in her sanctuary), he found provision with her, wholesome and ready prepared. He said: From where does this come to you? She said: It is from God; indeed God provides for whom He wills without reckoning (3:37).

When Zachariah saw this state, and God's kindness and gentleness towards her, it reminded him to ask God, Exalted, for the gift of a child at the very time when he despaired of it, and so he said: My Lord, grant me from Yourself a goodly offspring; indeed You are the Hearer of supplication (3:38).

Then the angels called to him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary: God gives you glad tidings of John, confirming a word from God, whose name, that is, the word which is from God, is Jesus son of Mary. So the glad tidings of this noble prophet included glad tidings of Jesus son of Mary, the confirmation of him and the testimony to his messengership. This word from God is a noble word with which God singled out Jesus son of Mary; otherwise it is one of the whole body of His words by which He brings creatures into being, as He, Exalted, said: Indeed the likeness of Jesus with God is as the likeness of Adam: He created him from dust, then said to him Be, and he was (3:59).

And His words: and a master and chaste, that is, this one of whom glad tidings are given, John, is a master among the most excellent and noble of the messengers. As for ḥaṣūr (chaste), it was said that it means one who has no children born to him and no desire for women; and it was said that it means one who is protected and guarded from sins and harmful desires, and this is the more fitting of the two meanings. And a prophet from among the righteous (3:39), those who have reached the highest summit of righteousness.

He said: My Lord, how shall I have a boy when old age has reached me and my wife is barren? These are two obstacles, so by what means, my Lord, shall this come about for me in the face of what contradicts it? He said: Thus; God does what He wills (3:40). For just as His wisdom requires that affairs run by their known causes, so He may break through that, because He is the Doer of what He intends, to whose power the causes have submitted and in which His will and His intent take effect; so no cause can defy His power, however great in strength it may be.

He said: My Lord, appoint for me a sign, so that joy and gladness may be obtained, even though I, my Lord, am certain of what You have told me; but the soul rejoices and the heart finds rest in the first tokens of mercy and kindness. He said: Your sign is that you shall not speak to people for three days except by gesture, and during this period remember your Lord much and glorify Him in the evening and the early morning (3:41), the beginning of the day and its end. So he was prevented from speech during this period, and there was in this a fitting correspondence to the coming of a child from between an aged old man and a barren woman; and his being unable to address human beings while his tongue ran freely with the remembrance and glorification of God was a further sign. Then at that point joy and gladness came to him, and he thanked God and multiplied his remembrance and glorification in the evenings and the early mornings.

This newborn was one of the blessings of Mary daughter of ʿImrān upon Zachariah, for the favour God had bestowed upon her of that wholesome provision which came without reckoning reminded him and stirred him to imploring and asking. God, Exalted, is the One who graciously grants both the cause and the thing caused, but He decrees beloved things at the hands of those whom He loves, so that God may raise their rank and magnify their reward.

Then He, Exalted, returned to the mention of Mary, and that she reached a mighty degree in worship and perfection, and so He, Exalted, said: And when the angels said: O Mary, indeed God has chosen you, that is, He has selected you and granted you majestic attributes and beautiful qualities; and purified you from base qualities; and chosen you above the women of the worlds (3:42). For this reason the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Many men attained perfection, but none of the women attained perfection except Mary daughter of ʿImrān, Āsiya daughter of Muzāḥim{{fn:The wife of Pharaoh.}} and Khadīja daughter of Khuwaylid; and the excellence of ʿĀʾisha over women is like the excellence of tharīd{{fn:A dish of bread sopped in meat broth, regarded by the Arabs as the finest of foods.}} over all other food."

So the angels called to her, at God's command to them to do so, that she might rejoice in God's blessings, give thanks to God, fulfil His rights and busy herself with His service. For this reason the angels said: O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, that is, multiply obedience, submission and humility before your Lord and persist in it; and prostrate and bow with those who bow (3:43), that is, pray with those who pray. So she carried out all that she was commanded, and she stood out and surpassed others in her perfection.

Since this story and others like it are among the greatest proofs of the messengership of Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him), in that he related it in detail and with accuracy, with neither addition nor omission, and that was only because it is revelation from God, the Mighty, the Wise, not something learnt from people, He, Exalted, said: That is of the tidings of the unseen which We reveal to you; and you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should take charge of Mary, when her mother brought her and they disputed over which of them should take charge of her, because she was the daughter of their leader and foremost man, and each of them desired goodness and reward from God, until the dispute brought them to the point of drawing lots over her: they cast their pens to draw lots, and the lot fell to Zachariah, as a mercy from God to him and to her.

So you, O Messenger, were not present at that scene to know it and relate it to people; rather God informed you of it. This is the greatest purpose in the narration of the stories: that a lesson be drawn from them, and the greatest of lessons is the use of them as evidence for the oneness of God, for messengership, for the resurrection and for the other great fundamentals.

When the angels said: O Mary, indeed God gives you glad tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, eminent in this world and the Hereafter and among those brought near (3:45): that is, he possesses eminence and great standing in this world and the Hereafter among created beings; and together with that he is, with God, among those brought near, who are the nearest of creatures to God and the highest of them in degree. This is a glad tiding which no other glad tiding resembles.

Part of the completeness of this glad tiding is that he would speak to people in the cradle, so that his speaking would be one of the signs of God and a mercy from Him to his mother and to created beings. Likewise he would speak to them in maturity, that is, in the state of his mature manhood, and this is the speech of prophethood, of calling and of guidance. His speech in the cradle contained signs and proofs of his truthfulness and his prophethood, and of his mother's innocence of the evil suspicions that were entertained about her; and his speech in his maturity contained his great benefit to created beings and his being an intermediary between them and their Lord in His revelation and in conveying His religion and His law. Together with that, he is among the righteous: those whose hearts God has made sound through knowledge of Him and love of Him, whose tongues He has made sound through praising Him and remembering Him, and whose limbs He has made sound through obeying Him and serving Him.

She said: My Lord, how shall I have a child when no human being has touched me? This is one of the things that provoke astonishment. He said: Thus; God creates what He wills, so that the servants may know that He has power over all things and that nothing can resist His will: when He decrees a matter, He only says to it Be, and it is (3:47).
And He will teach him the Book, that is, the whole class of the earlier scriptures, and judgement between people, and He will give him prophethood.

And He will make him a messenger to the Children of Israel and support him with clear signs and overwhelming proofs, in that he said: I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, which shows you that I am truly the messenger of God, and that is that I create for you out of clay the form of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by God's leave; and I heal the one born blind, which is the one whose eyes are effaced, who has lost his sight and his eyes, and the leper, and I give life to the dead by God's leave, and I inform you of what you eat and what you store up in your houses. Indeed in that, which has been mentioned, is a sign for you, if you are believers (3:49).

And confirming what is before me of the Torah. So God supported him with two kinds of signs and proofs: the extraordinary, astonishing miracles which none but the prophets are able to bring, and the message, the call and the religion that he brought, and the fact that it is the religion of the Torah and the religion of the earlier prophets. This is the greatest of the proofs of the truthfulness of the truthful, for had he been one of the liars he would have opposed what the messengers brought and contradicted them in their fundamentals and their branches. By this it is known that he is the messenger of God and that what he brought is truth in which there is no doubt. And likewise his words: and to make lawful to you some of what was forbidden to you, that is, and to lighten for you some of the burdens and the shackles; so fear God and obey me (3:50).

Indeed God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is what all the messengers call to: the worship of God alone, without partner, and obedience to them. This is the straight path which brings whoever travels it to the Gardens of bliss.

Then at that point the factions of the Children of Israel differed concerning Jesus: among them were those who believed in him and followed him, and among them were those who disbelieved in him, denied him and accused his mother of indecency, like the Jews. Then when Jesus perceived disbelief from them, and their agreement upon rejecting his call, he said, summoning the Children of Israel to support him: Who are my helpers towards God? The disciples said, that is, the helpers: We are the helpers of God; we believe in God, so bear witness that we are Muslims (3:52). This was one of God's favours upon them and upon Jesus, in that He inspired these disciples to believe in him, to submit to his obedience and to support His messenger.

Our Lord, we believe in what You have sent down and we follow the Messenger. This is a complete commitment to faith in all that God has sent down and to obedience to His messenger. So write us down among those who bear witness (3:53): to You, of Your oneness; to Your prophet, of his messengership; and to Your religion, that it is true and right.

As for those from whom Jesus perceived disbelief, who were the majority of the Children of Israel, they plotted against Jesus, and God plotted against them, and God is the best of plotters (3:54). They agreed upon killing him and crucifying him, but the likeness of Jesus was cast upon another for them, and so they seized the one upon whom his likeness had been cast for them.

When God said: O Jesus, I am going to take you and raise you to Myself and purify you from those who disbelieve. So God raised His servant and messenger Jesus to Himself, and his likeness was cast upon another. They seized the one upon whom his likeness had been cast, killed him and crucified him, and they incurred a mighty sin through their intention that he was the messenger of God. God said: And they did not kill him and did not crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them (4:157).

In this verse is evidence of the exaltation of God, Exalted, and of His rising over His Throne in reality, as the texts of the Qur'an and the hadith of the Prophet show, which the people of the Sunna received with acceptance, faith and submission. God is Mighty, Strong and Overpowering, and of His might is that He restrained the Children of Israel from killing Jesus (peace be upon him) after their firm resolve, when nothing stood in their way, as He said, Exalted: And when I restrained the Children of Israel from you when you came to them with the clear proofs, and those who disbelieved among them said: This is nothing but plain magic (5:110). He is Wise, putting things in their places, and He had the greatest wisdom in casting the likeness upon the Children of Israel, so they fell into confusion, as He said, Exalted: And indeed those who differ concerning him are in doubt about it; they have no knowledge of it except the following of conjecture, and they did not kill him for certain (4:157).

Then He said, Exalted: and I am going to make those who follow you above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. It has been said before that God supported the believers among them against the disbelievers. Then the Christians, who trace themselves to Jesus (peace be upon him), did not cease to prevail over the Jews, since the Christians were nearer to following Jesus than the Jews were, until God sent our Prophet Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him). Then the Muslims were the true followers of Jesus, and God supported them and gave them victory over the Jews, the Christians and the rest of the disbelievers. When the disbelievers, Christians and others, are at some times given the upper hand over the Muslims, it is only wisdom from God and a punishment for their leaving the following of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him).

Then to Me is your return, that is, the destination of all creatures, and I shall judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ (3:55): each claims that the truth is with him, that he is right and the other wrong, and these are mere claims that need proof.

I say: then He made clear what He would do with them, and said: As for those who disbelieve, I shall punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they shall have no helpers (3:56).

And as for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will pay them their rewards in full; and God does not love the wrongdoers (3:57). This recompense is general for everyone who is characterised by these attributes from among all the people of the earlier religions. Then, when the master of the messengers and seal of the prophets was sent, and his message abrogated all the messages and his religion abrogated all the religions, whoever holds to any religion other than this one became one of those who perish.
And His words, Exalted:

That is: this mighty Qur'an, which contains the tidings of the first and the last, of the prophets and the messengers, is the clear signs of God; it is that which reminds the servants of everything they need, and it is the wise, the firmly established, truthful in its reports and good in its rulings.

When He had mentioned the story of Mary and Jesus and the true tidings of them both, and that he is a servant upon whom God bestowed favour, and that whoever claims there is anything of divinity in him has lied against God, given the lie to all His prophets and given the lie to Jesus (peace and blessings be upon him): the doubt that presented itself to those who took him as a god is a false doubt, for had it any sound basis, Adam would have had a better claim to it than he, since he was created without mother or father; yet despite that all mankind agree that he is one of the servants of God. So the claim that Jesus is divine because he was created from a mother without a father is one of the most false of claims.
This is the truth in which there is no doubt: that Jesus is as he said of himself: I said to them nothing except what You commanded me: Worship God, my Lord and your Lord (5:117).

A delegation of the Christians of Najrān had come to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and they had hardened themselves in their falsehood after the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) had set before them the proofs that Jesus is the servant of God and His messenger, since they claimed his divinity. Matters between him and them reached the point where God, Exalted, commanded him to invoke a mutual curse (mubāhala) with them, for the truth had become plain to them but obstinacy and partisanship kept them from it. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) called them to the mutual imprecation: that he should come with his household and his sons, and they should come with their households and their sons, and then they would pray to God, Exalted, to send down His punishment and His curse upon the liars. They consulted among themselves whether to accept this from him, and their opinion settled on not accepting it, because they knew that he was truly the prophet of God and that if they imprecated against him they would perish, they and their children and their households. So they made peace with him, offered him the poll-tax (jizya) and asked him for a truce and a treaty, and he (peace and blessings be upon him) granted them that and did not press them hard, because the purpose had been achieved in the clarity of the truth and the exposure of their obstinacy, since they resolved to refuse the mutual imprecation; and that demonstrates that they were wrongdoers.

For this reason He, Exalted, said: Indeed this is the true narrative, that is, that in which there is no doubt; and indeed God is surely the Mighty, who by His power and strength has subdued all existing things, and to whom the inhabitants of the earth and the heavens have submitted; and together with that He is the Wise (3:62), who puts things in their proper places and sets them down in their proper stations.

This noble verse was one the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to write to the kings of the People of the Book. He would sometimes recite in the first unit (rakʿa) of the voluntary dawn prayer Say: We believe in God (2:136), to the end of the verse, and recite this verse in the final unit of the voluntary morning prayer, because it contains the call to a single religion upon which the prophets and messengers agreed, and because it embodies the oneness of divinity (tawḥīd al-ilāhiyya) which is built upon the worship of God alone without partner, and upon the belief that human beings and all created things, every one of them, are at the level of created humanity, and none of them deserves anything of the particular attributes of lordship or the qualities of divinity. If the People of the Book and others submit to this, they are guided; but if they turn away, then say: Bear witness that we are Muslims (3:64), like His words, Exalted: Say: O disbelievers (109:1), to the end of the sūra.

When He had mentioned their corrupt objection, He informed that it was nothing strange in their conduct; rather there had gone before from them ugly precedents greater than the course they took with the Messenger in whom they claim to believe: their asking him to see God openly with their eyes; their taking the calf as a god to worship after they had seen with their own eyes signs that no one else had seen; their refusal to accept the rulings of their scripture, the Torah, until the Mount was raised above their heads and they were threatened that if they did not believe it would be dropped upon them, whereupon they accepted it with reluctance and with a faith resembling forced faith; their refusal to enter the gates of the town which they were commanded to enter prostrating and seeking forgiveness, so that they went against it in word and deed; the transgression of those among them who transgressed on the Sabbath, for which God punished them with that hideous punishment; the taking of the firm covenant from them, which they cast behind their backs, disbelieving in the signs of God and killing His messengers without right; their saying that they killed the Messiah, Jesus, and crucified him, when in fact they neither killed him nor crucified him, but another was made to appear to them in his likeness, so that they killed and crucified someone else; their claim that their hearts are wrapped and do not grasp or understand what you say to them; their turning people away from the path of God, so that they turned them away from the truth and called them to the error and misguidance they themselves were upon; and their taking of unlawful gain and usury despite God's prohibition of it to them and His severity concerning it. Those who did these deeds, then, cannot be thought strange for asking the Messenger Muḥammad to bring down upon them a book from heaven.

This method is one of the best methods for disputing with an opponent who is in the wrong: when a false objection issues from him which he makes into a doubt for himself and for others in rejecting the truth, there is laid bare of his vile condition and his hideous deeds what is among the ugliest things that have issued from him, so that everyone may know that this objection is from that same base valley, and that it has precedents alongside which this one is to be placed. Likewise every objection they raise against the prophethood of Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) can be met with its like, or with something stronger than it, concerning the prophethood of the one in whom they claim to believe, so that by this their evil is held in check and their falsehood is suppressed; and every argument they follow in establishing the prophethood of the one in whom they believe, it and its counterpart and what is stronger than it indicate and establish the prophethood of Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him).

Since the purpose of enumerating those of their abominations which God enumerated was this confrontation, He did not expound them at length in this place, but alluded to them and referred to the places where they occur; He has expounded them elsewhere, in the place fitting for their exposition.

And His words: And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in him before his death. It is possible that the pronoun here in His words before his death refers back to the People of the Book, in which case every person of the Book whom death attends and who witnesses the matter in reality will believe in Jesus (peace be upon him), but with a faith that does not benefit, a faith of compulsion. The purport of this would then be a threat and a warning to them not to persist in this condition which they will regret before their deaths; so how will their condition be on the day of their gathering and their rising?! And it is possible that the pronoun in His words before his death refers to Jesus (peace be upon him), in which case the meaning is: there is no one of the People of the Book but will surely believe in the Messiah (peace be upon him) before the death of the Messiah; and that will be when the Hour draws near and its great signs appear, for the sound ḥadīths have multiplied concerning his descent (peace be upon him) at the end of this community: he will kill the Antichrist (al-Dajjāl), abolish the poll-tax, and the People of the Book will believe in him together with the believers. And on the Day of Resurrection Jesus will be a witness against them, testifying against them concerning their deeds, whether they were in accordance with God's law or not. At that time he will testify to nothing but the falsity of everything they were upon that contradicts the law of the Qur'an and what Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) called them to. We know this because of our knowledge of the perfect justice of the Messiah (peace be upon him) and his truthfulness, and that he testifies only to the truth; and the truth is none other than that what Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) brought is the truth, and whatever is besides it is error and falsehood.

When God said: O Jesus son of Mary, remember My favour upon you and upon your mother, that is, remember it with your heart and your tongue, and discharge its due in gratitude to your Lord, since He bestowed upon you favours He bestowed upon no one else: when I supported you with the Holy Spirit, that is, when I strengthened you with the spirit and the revelation which purified you and made you grow, so that you came to have strength for carrying out God's command and calling to His path. It was also said that what is meant by the Holy Spirit is Gabriel (peace be upon him), and that God aided him through him, through his constant attendance upon him and his steadying him in trying situations. You spoke to people in the cradle and in maturity: what is meant by speaking here is not the ordinary speaking which is mere talk; rather what is meant by it is the speech by which both the speaker and the one addressed benefit, namely the call to God. Jesus (peace be upon him) had of this what his brothers among the messengers of firm resolve had, namely speaking in the state of maturity with the message, the call to good and the forbidding of evil; and he was distinguished from them in that he spoke to people in the cradle, saying: Indeed I am the servant of God; He has given me the Book and made me a prophet, and He has made me blessed wherever I may be, and has enjoined upon me prayer and alms-giving as long as I live (19:30–31), to the end of the verse.

And when I taught you the Book and wisdom. The Book includes the earlier scriptures, and especially the Torah, for he was among the most knowledgeable of the prophets of the Children of Israel concerning it after Moses; and it includes the Gospel which God sent down to him. Wisdom is knowledge of the secrets of the law, its benefits and its underlying purposes, excellence in calling and teaching, and attending to what ought to be done in the manner in which it ought to be done. And when you created out of clay the form of a bird, that is, a bird fashioned in shape with no spirit in it, then breathed into it and it became a bird by My leave; and you healed the one born blind, who has neither sight nor eye, and the leper by My leave; and when you brought forth the dead by My leave. These are clear signs and dazzling miracles before which physicians and others are powerless; God supported Jesus with them and strengthened his call by them. And when I restrained the Children of Israel from you when you came to them with clear proofs, and those of them who disbelieved said, when the truth came to them supported by the clear proofs that necessitate faith in it: This is nothing but manifest sorcery (5:110). They resolved to kill Jesus and strove to do so, but God restrained their hands from him, protected him from them and kept him safe.

These, then, are favours which God graciously bestowed upon His servant and messenger Jesus son of Mary, and He called him to give thanks for them and to discharge their due; and he (upon him be blessings and peace) discharged them most completely, and was patient as his brothers among the messengers of firm resolve were patient.

That is: and remember My favour upon you when I made easy for you followers and helpers, for I inspired the disciples, that is, I put it into them and disposed their hearts to faith in Me and in My messenger; or I revealed to them through your tongue, that is, I commanded them by the revelation that came to you from God. They responded to that and submitted and said: We believe, so bear witness that we are Muslims (5:111). So they combined outward submission (islām) and compliance through righteous deeds with inward faith, which brings its possessor out of hypocrisy and out of weakness of faith.
The disciples (ḥawāriyyūn) are the helpers, as Jesus son of Mary said to the disciples: Who are my helpers towards God? The disciples said: We are the helpers of God (61:14).

When the disciples said: O Jesus son of Mary, is your Lord able to send down to us a table from heaven?, that is, a table with food upon it. This on their part was not out of any doubt concerning God's power and His ability to do that; it was rather by way of a request and courtesy from them. And since asking for signs of one's own proposing is contrary to submission to the truth, and these words issuing from the disciples might have given that impression, Jesus (peace be upon him) admonished them and said: Fear God, if you are believers (5:112), for the faith a believer has carries him to constant God-fearing and to submitting to God's command, and he does not ask for signs of his own proposing, of which he does not know what will come after them.

So the disciples informed him that their purpose was not this meaning; rather they had righteous purposes, and it was on account of their need for it. They said: We desire to eat of it, which is evidence that they were in need of it; and that our hearts be at rest in faith when we see the signs with our own eyes, so that faith becomes the very certainty of sight (ʿayn al-yaqīn), just as the Friend of God, Abraham (upon him be blessings and peace), asked his Lord to show him how He gives life to the dead: He said: Have you not believed? He said: Yes, but so that my heart may be at rest (2:260). The servant is in need of increase in knowledge, certainty and faith at every moment, and for this reason they said: and that we may know that you have told us the truth, that is, that we may know the truth of what you have brought, that it is real and true; and that we may be among the witnesses to it (5:113), so that it may be a benefit for those who come after us: we bear witness to it for you, the proof is established and additional demonstration is obtained thereby.

When Jesus (upon him be blessings and peace) heard that and knew their purpose, he granted their request in that matter and said: O God, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven, that it may be a festival for us, for the first of us and the last of us, and a sign from You, that is, that the time of its descent may be a festival and a season by which this mighty sign is remembered, so that it is preserved and not forgotten with the passing of time and the recurrence of the years, just as God, Exalted, made the festivals of the Muslims and their rites reminders of His signs, pointers to the ways of the messengers and their upright paths and to His favour and beneficence towards them. And provide for us, for You are the best of providers (5:114), that is, make it provision for us. So Jesus (peace be upon him) asked for its descent and that it be for these two benefits: the benefit of religion, in that it be an abiding sign, and the benefit of this world, namely that it be provision.

God said: I am going to send it down to you; but whoever of you disbelieves after that, I shall punish him with a punishment with which I do not punish anyone among the worlds (5:115), because he witnessed the dazzling sign and disbelieved out of obstinacy and wrongdoing, and so deserved the painful punishment and the severe chastisement.

Know that God, Exalted, promised that He would send it down and threatened them with this warning if they disbelieved, but He did not mention that He sent it down. It is possible that He did not send it down because they did not choose that, and indicating this is the fact that it is not mentioned in the Gospel that the Christians have in their hands, nor has it any existence there. And it is possible that it descended as God promised, for He does not break His promise, and that the absence of its mention in the Gospels in their hands is part of the portion of which they were reminded but which they forgot; or that it was not mentioned in the Gospel at all, but was rather handed down among them, the later generations transmitting it from the earlier, so that God was content with that in place of mentioning it in the Gospel. Indicating this meaning are His words: and that we may be among the witnesses to it (5:113). And God knows best the reality of the matter.

And when God said: O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides God? This is a rebuke to the Christians who said that God is the third of three! God says these words to Jesus, and Jesus disavows it and says: Glory be to You, far above these ugly words and above what does not befit You; it is not for me to say what I have no right to, that is, it is not proper or fitting for me to say anything that is not among my attributes or my rights. For no created being, neither the angels brought near, nor the prophets sent as messengers, nor anyone else, has any right or entitlement to the station of divinity; rather all are servants who are governed, creatures who are subjected, needy and powerless. If I had said it, You would have known it; You know what is in my self, and I do not know what is in Your Self. You know best what has issued from me, for You are the Knower of the unseen. This is part of the perfect courtesy of the Messiah (upon him be blessings and peace) in addressing his Lord: he (peace be upon him) did not say, I did not say anything of that; rather he spoke words that deny of himself the saying of any statement contrary to his noble station, and that this is among impossible things, and he declared his Lord utterly far above that, and referred knowledge back to the Knower of the unseen and the seen.

Then he stated explicitly what he had commanded the Children of Israel, and said: I said to them nothing except what You commanded me: for I am a servant who follows Your command, not one who ventures boldly against Your majesty; Worship God, my Lord and your Lord, that is, I commanded them nothing but the worship of God alone and the devoting of religion sincerely to Him, which includes the prohibition of taking me and my mother as two gods besides God and the declaration that I am a servant who has a Lord: just as He is your Lord, so He is my Lord. And I was a witness over them as long as I remained among them: I bear witness as to who carried out this command and who did not carry it out. Then when You took me up, You were the Watcher over them, that is, the One acquainted with their secrets and their inner thoughts; and You are Witness over all things (5:117), in knowledge, hearing and sight: Your knowledge has encompassed all things known, Your hearing all things heard, and Your sight all things seen; so You are the One who recompenses Your servants for what You know in them of good and evil.

If You punish them, they are Your servants: and You are more merciful to them than they are to themselves, and more knowing of their states; so were it not that they are rebellious servants, You would not punish them. And if You forgive them, You are the Mighty, that is, Your forgiveness issues from complete might and power, not like one who forgives and pardons out of incapacity and lack of power; the Wise (5:118), in that it is among the requirements of Your wisdom that You forgive whoever brings the means of forgiveness.

God said, making plain the condition of His servants on the Day of Resurrection, which of them is the successful and which the ruined, which the wretched and which the blessed: This is the Day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness. The truthful are those whose deeds, words and intentions were upright upon the straight path and the right guidance; on the Day of Resurrection they find the fruit of that truthfulness when God settles them in a seat of truth with a Sovereign Omnipotent. For this reason He said: For them are Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever; God is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him. That is the great success (5:119). The liars are their opposite: they will find the harm of their lying and their fabrication and the fruit of their corrupt deeds.

To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, because He is the Creator of them both and the Governor of all that, by His decree of destiny, His decree of law and His decree of recompense. For this reason He said: and He has power over all things (5:120): nothing is beyond Him; rather all things are submissive to His will and subjected to His command.

When He had mentioned the story of Zachariah and John, which was one of the wondrous signs, He moved on from it to what is more wondrous still, by degrees, from the lesser to the greater, and said: And mention in the Book, the noble Book, Mary (peace be upon her). This is among the greatest of her merits: that she is mentioned in the mighty Book which the Muslims recite in the east of the earth and its west, mentioned in it with the finest mention and the most excellent praise, as a reward for her excellent work and her perfect striving. That is: and mention in the Book Mary in her goodly state, when she withdrew, that is, she went far away from her family, to an eastern place (19:16), that is, on the side towards the east from them.

And she took, apart from them, a screen, that is, a covering and a barrier. This withdrawal of hers and her taking a screen were so that she might seclude herself and be alone in the worship of her Lord, and be devoutly obedient to Him in a state of sincerity, submission and lowliness before God, Exalted. That was in compliance on her part with His words, Exalted: And when the angels said: O Mary, indeed God has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds. O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord and prostrate and bow with those who bow (3:42–43). And His words: Then We sent to her Our Spirit, who is Gabriel (peace be upon him), and he took for her the form of a well-proportioned human being (19:17), that is, a perfect man in a beautiful appearance and a goodly form, with no defect or deficiency in him, because she could not have borne the sight of him as he really is.

When she saw him in this state, while she was secluded from her family and alone away from people, having taken a screen even against the dearest of people to her, namely her family, she feared that he was a man who had come upon her with evil intent and desired her, so she sought protection in her Lord and sought refuge from him.

She said to him: I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, that is, I take shelter in Him and hold fast to His mercy, lest you reach me with any harm; if you are God-fearing (19:18), that is, if you fear God and act in fear of Him, then leave off approaching me. So she combined seeking protection in her Lord with making him afraid and warning him, and commanding him to hold to the fear of God. She was in that solitary situation, in youth and far from people, and he was in that dazzling beauty and that perfect, well-proportioned human form, yet he had not uttered any evil to her or made any advance towards her; it was only fear on her part. This is the utmost that can be of chastity and distance from evil and its causes. This chastity, especially given the conjunction of the motives and the absence of anything to prevent, is among the most excellent of deeds, and for this reason God praised her and said: And Mary daughter of ʿImrān, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into it of Our Spirit (66:12), and: And she who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our Spirit and made her and her son a sign for the worlds (21:91). So God recompensed her for her chastity with a child who was one of the signs of God and a messenger among His messengers.

When Gabriel saw her alarm and fear, he said: I am only a messenger of your Lord, that is, my function and my business is only to carry out my Lord's message concerning you, to grant you a pure boy (19:19). This is a great glad tiding of the child and of his purity, for purity entails his being cleansed of blameworthy traits and his being characterised by praiseworthy traits.

She marvelled at the existence of a child without a father, and said: How shall I have a boy when no human being has touched me and I have not been unchaste? (19:20) For a child comes into existence only by that means.

He said: Thus; your Lord has said: It is easy for Me, and that We may make him a sign for people, pointing to the perfection of the power of God, Exalted, and to the fact that none of the causes has independent effect of itself; rather their effect is by God's determination. So He shows His servants the breaking of the customary order in some of the ordinary causes, lest they stop short at the causes and cut off their regard from the One who determines them and brings them about. And a mercy from Us, that is, and that We may make him a mercy from Us to him, to his mother and to people. As for God's mercy to him, it is because God singled him out with His revelation and bestowed upon him what He bestowed upon the messengers of firm resolve. As for His mercy to his mother, it is because of the honour, the fair praise and the great benefits that came to her. As for His mercy to people, the greatest of His favours upon them is that He sent among them a messenger who recites to them His signs, purifies them and teaches them the Book and wisdom, so that they believe in him and obey him, and the happiness of this world and the Hereafter is obtained for them. And it was, that is, the existence of Jesus (peace be upon him) in this manner, a matter decreed (19:21), a prior decree; so this determination and decree had of necessity to take effect, and Gabriel (peace be upon him) breathed into the opening of her garment.
That is: when she conceived Jesus (peace be upon him), she feared disgrace, and so she withdrew far from people to a distant place.

When her delivery drew near, the pangs of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. When the pain of childbirth hurt her, together with the pain of being cut off from food and drink and the pain in her heart at what people would say, and she feared she would not be able to bear it, she wished that she had died before this event and had been a thing forgotten, utterly forgotten, so that she would not be mentioned. This wish was on account of that distressing situation, and there was no good or benefit for her in this wish; the good and the benefit lay rather in the decree of what came to pass.

Then at that point the angel calmed her alarm and steadied her heart, and called to her from beneath her, perhaps from a place lower than her place, and said to her: Do not grieve, that is, do not be distressed or anxious, for your Lord has placed beneath you a stream (19:24), that is, a river from which you may drink.
And shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you fresh ripe dates (19:25), that is, fresh, delicious and nourishing.

So eat, of the dates, and drink, from the river, and be comforted in eye, with Jesus. This was her reassurance as regards safety from the pain of childbirth and the obtaining of wholesome food and drink. As for what people would say, He commanded her that if she saw any human being she should say, by way of gesture: I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, that is, silence, so I shall not speak today to any human being (19:26), that is, do not address them with speech, so that you may be relieved of their talk and their words; and it was known among them that silence was one of the prescribed acts of worship. She was not commanded to address them in denial of that concerning herself only because people would not believe her and there was no benefit in it, and so that her exoneration by the speech of Jesus in the cradle might be the greatest witness to her innocence. For a woman's bringing a child without a husband, and her claiming that it was from no one, is among the greatest of claims, such that even if a number of witnesses were produced it would not be believed; so the proof of this breach of the customary order was made something of the same kind, namely the speech of Jesus while he was still very small.
For this reason He, Exalted, said:

That is: when Mary had recovered from her confinement, she came to her people with Jesus, carrying him. That was because of her knowledge of her own innocence and purity, so she came unconcerned and untroubled. They said: You have indeed brought an unheard-of thing (19:27), that is, something grave and disastrous; and by that they meant unchastity, far be she from that.

O sister of Aaron: the apparent meaning is that he was a real brother of hers, and so they attributed her to him. Your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste (19:28), that is, your parents were nothing but righteous, free of evil, and especially this evil to which they were pointing. Their intent was: how then are you unlike the two of them in character, and have done what they never did?! That is because offspring for the most part take after one another in righteousness and its opposite, so they marvelled, in accordance with what arose in their hearts, at how this had come from her.

So she pointed them to him, that is, speak to him. She pointed only because she had been commanded, when people addressed her, to say: I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, so I shall not speak today to any human being (19:26). When she indicated to them that they should speak to him, they marvelled at that and said: How shall we speak to one who is a child in the cradle? (19:29), because that had never been the customary way of things nor had it ever come from anyone at that age.

Then at that point Jesus (peace be upon him) said, while he was a child in the cradle: Indeed I am the servant of God; He has given me the Book and made me a prophet (19:30). So he addressed them describing himself as a servant, and that there was in him no attribute by which he would deserve to be a god or a son of God. Exalted is God above the saying of the Christians, who contradict Jesus in his words Indeed I am the servant of God while claiming to agree with him. He has given me the Book, that is, He has decreed that He will give me the Book, and made me a prophet (19:30). So he informed them that he is the servant of God, and that God taught him the Book and made him one of the company of His prophets; this is from his perfecting of himself.
Then he mentioned his perfecting of others, and said:

And He has made me blessed wherever I may be, that is, in whatever place and whatever time. The blessing God placed in me consists in teaching good and calling to it, forbidding evil and calling to God in his words and his deeds; so everyone who sat with him or met with him received his blessing, and his companion was made happy through him. And He has enjoined upon me prayer and alms-giving as long as I live (19:31), that is, He has enjoined upon me the fulfilment of His rights, the greatest of which is prayer, and the rights of His servants, the most important of which is alms-giving, for the duration of my life; that is, I comply with my Lord's injunction, acting upon it and carrying it out.

And He has enjoined upon me also that I be dutiful to my mother, treating her with the utmost kindness and discharging what is due to her, on account of her nobility and her excellence, and because she is a mother who has the right of motherhood and what follows from it. And He has not made me arrogant, that is, haughty towards God and self-exalting over His servants, or wretched (19:32), in my worldly life or my Hereafter. He has not made me so; rather He has made me obedient to Him, submissive, humble, lowly and modest towards the servants of God, happy in this world and the Hereafter, I and whoever follows me.

When perfection and praiseworthy traits had been completed for him, he said: And peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die and the day I am raised up alive (19:33), that is, by the grace of my Lord and His generosity, safety from evil, from Satan and from punishment has come to me on the day of my birth, the day of my death and the day of my resurrection. That entails his safety from the terrors and from the abode of the wicked, and that he is among the people of the Abode of Peace. This, then, is a mighty miracle and a dazzling proof that he is truly the messenger of God and the servant of God.

That is: that one who is described with those attributes is Jesus son of Mary, without doubt or uncertainty; rather it is the word of truth, and the speech of God, than which none is more truthful in saying or finer in discourse. This, then, is the certain report concerning Jesus (peace be upon him), and whatever has been said of him that contradicts this is definitely false, and at most it is doubt on the part of the one who says it, who has no knowledge of it. For this reason He said: about which they are in doubt (19:34), that is, they doubt, and so they dispute on the basis of their doubt and argue on the basis of their guessing. Among them is one who says of him that he is God, or the son of God, or the third of three. Exalted is God above their falsehood and their fabrication, in great exaltation.

So it is not for God to take any son, that is, it is not proper or fitting, because that is among impossible things, for He is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy, the Owner of all dominions; how then should He take from among His servants and His possessions a son? Glory be to Him, that is, He is transcendent and holy, far above having a son and above any deficiency. When He decrees a matter, that is, any matter, small or great, it is neither impossible for Him nor difficult; He only says to it Be, and it is (19:35). So when His determination and His will take effect in the upper world and the lower, how should He have a son?! And when it is the case that, when He intends a thing, He says to it Be, and it is, how can His bringing Jesus into existence without a father be thought improbable?!

For this reason Jesus declared that he is a servant with a Lord, like everyone else, and said: And indeed God is my Lord and your Lord, who created us and fashioned us, whose governance takes effect in us and whose determination disposes of us; so worship Him, that is, devote worship sincerely to Him and strive in turning to Him in repentance. In this is the affirmation of the oneness of lordship (tawḥīd al-rubūbiyya) and the oneness of divinity (tawḥīd al-ilāhiyya), and the use of the first as evidence for the second. For this reason he said: This is a straight path (19:36), that is, an even path leading to God, since it is the path of the messengers and their followers; and whatever is other than this is among the paths of misguidance and error.

When He, Exalted, had made plain the condition of Jesus son of Mary, concerning which there is no doubt or uncertainty, He informed that the factions, that is, the sects of misguidance among the Jews, the Christians and others, in their various classes, differed concerning Jesus (peace be upon him): some went to excess regarding him and some fell short. Among them were those who said that he is God! Among them were those who said that he is the son of God! Among them were those who said that he is the third of three! And among them were those who did not make him a messenger at all, but accused him of being the child of fornication, like the Jews! The sayings of all of these are false and their opinions corrupt, built upon doubt and obstinacy, upon corrupt proofs and worthless doubts, and all of these deserve the severe threat. For this reason He said: So woe to those who disbelieve, in God, His messengers and His books, among whom are included the Jews and the Christians who say of Jesus the saying of disbelief, from the witnessing of a mighty Day (19:37), that is, the witnessing of the Day of Resurrection, which the first and the last will witness, the inhabitants of the heavens and the inhabitants of the earth, the Creator and the created, a Day filled with convulsions and terrors, comprising the recompense for deeds. Then at that time will become clear what they used to conceal and what they used to disclose, and what they used to hide.

That is: and mention Mary (peace be upon her), praising her, making plain her worth and proclaiming her nobility, and so He said: And she who guarded her chastity, that is, she kept it from what is unlawful and from approaching it, and indeed even from what is lawful, for she did not marry, because of her occupation with worship and her time being wholly taken up with the service of her Lord. And when Gabriel came to her in the form of a well-proportioned human being, perfect in form and beauty, she said: I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing (19:18). So God recompensed her with the like of her deed and granted her a child without a father; rather Gabriel (peace be upon him) breathed into her, and she conceived by God's leave. And We made her and her son a sign for the worlds (21:91), in that she conceived him and gave birth to him without anyone having touched her; in that he spoke in the cradle and cleared her of what the accusers suspected of her, and told of himself in that state; and in that God caused to be wrought at his hands the extraordinary deeds and miracles that are well known. So she and her son were a sign for the worlds, spoken of generation after generation, and from which those who take heed draw their lesson.

That is: and We bestowed favour upon Jesus son of Mary and made him and his mother among the wondrous signs of God, in that she conceived him and gave birth to him without a father, and he spoke in the cradle as a child, and God caused to be wrought at his hands the signs that He wrought. And We gave them both refuge on a height, that is, an elevated place, and this, and God knows best, was at the time of her delivery, having a place of rest, that is, a settled abode and ease, and a flowing spring (23:50), that is, running water, as shown by His words: your Lord has placed beneath you, that is, beneath the place in which you are, because of its elevation, a stream (19:24), that is, a river, which is the flowing spring; and shake towards you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you fresh ripe dates. So eat and drink and be comforted in eye (19:24–26).

He, Exalted, says: And when the son of Mary was cited as an example, that is, when his worship was forbidden and his worship was placed on the same footing as the worship of idols and rivals, behold, your people, those who deny you, at it, that is, on account of this example that was cited, raise a clamour (43:57), that is, they persist in their dispute with you, shout, and claim that they have prevailed and triumphed in their argument.

And they said: Are our gods better, or is he?, meaning Jesus, since the worship of all of them was forbidden and they were joined together in the threat against whoever worships them; and there was also revealed His words, Exalted: Indeed you and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell; you shall come to it (21:98). The form of their wrongful argument was that they said: it is established with us and with you, O Muḥammad, that Jesus is one of the servants of God brought near, who have the good final outcome; so why have you made him and our objects of worship equal in forbidding the worship of all of them?! Were your argument not false, it would not be self-contradictory! And why did you say: Indeed you and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell; you shall come to it (21:98)?! This wording, according to their claim, includes both the idols and Jesus; so is this anything but a contradiction? And the contradiction of an argument is evidence of its falsity! This is the furthest extent of what they adduce in establishing this doubt, over which they rejoiced and were glad, and began to raise a clamour and congratulate one another. Yet it is, praise be to God, among the weakest and most false of doubts; for God's placing the prohibition of worshipping the Messiah on the same footing as the prohibition of worshipping idols is because worship is the right of God, Exalted, which none of created beings deserves, neither the angels brought near, nor the prophets sent as messengers, nor any created being besides them; so what doubt is there in making the prohibition of worshipping Jesus and the prohibition of worshipping others equal?!

The superiority of Jesus (peace be upon him) and his being brought near to his Lord contain nothing that indicates a difference between him and them in this respect; he is only as He, Exalted, said: He was no more than a servant upon whom We bestowed favour, of prophethood, wisdom, knowledge and action, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel (43:59), by which they recognise the power of God, Exalted, to bring him into existence without a father. As for His words, Exalted, Indeed you and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell; you shall come to it (21:98), the answer concerning it is from three aspects:
- The first: that in His words Indeed you and what you worship besides God, the word what (mā) is a noun used for that which lacks reason, and the Messiah and his like do not fall under it.
- The second: that the address is to the polytheists who were in Mecca and its surroundings, and they worshipped only idols and graven images, and did not worship the Messiah.

- The third: that God said after this verse: Indeed those for whom the best has gone forth from Us, they shall be kept far from it (21:101); and there is no doubt that Jesus and the other prophets and friends of God are included in this verse.

Then He, Exalted, said: And if We willed, We could have made from you angels in the earth, succeeding one another (43:60), that is, We could have made in your place angels who would succeed you in the earth and would be in the earth, so that We would send to them angels of their own kind. As for you, O company of human beings, you cannot bear that angels be sent to you; so it is of God's mercy towards you that He sent to you messengers of your own kind, from whom you are able to receive.

And indeed he is a sign of the Hour, that is, Jesus (peace be upon him) is indeed a proof of the Hour, and that the One who is able to bring him into existence from a mother without a father is able to raise the dead from their graves; or: Jesus (peace be upon him) will indeed descend at the end of time, and his descent will be one of the signs of the Hour. So do not doubt it, that is, do not doubt the coming of the Hour, for doubting it is disbelief; and follow me, by complying with what I have commanded you and avoiding what I have forbidden you; this is a straight path (43:61), leading to God, Mighty and Majestic.
And let not Satan turn you away, from what God has commanded you; indeed he, that is, Satan, is to you a manifest enemy (43:62), eager to lead you astray, expending his utmost effort in that.

And when Jesus came with the clear proofs, which indicate the truth of his prophethood and the soundness of what he brought them, such as giving life to the dead, healing the one born blind and the leper, and other such signs, he said, to the Children of Israel: I have come to you with wisdom, prophethood and the knowledge of what ought to be done in the manner in which it ought to be done, and to make clear to you some of that over which you differ, that is, I make clear to you the correct position in it and the answer to it, so that by this the confusion is removed from you. So he (peace be upon him) came completing and perfecting the law of Moses (peace be upon him) and the rulings of the Torah, and brought some alleviations that called for submission to him and acceptance of what he brought them. So fear God and obey me (43:63), that is, worship God alone, without partner, comply with His command, avoid His prohibition, believe in me and affirm my truthfulness, and obey me (43:63).

Indeed God, He is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is a straight path (43:64). In this is the affirmation of the oneness of lordship (tawḥīd al-rubūbiyya), in that God is the One who nurtures all His creation with blessings of every kind, outward and inward; the affirmation of the oneness of worship (tawḥīd al-ʿubūdiyya), through the command to worship God alone, without partner; the declaration by Jesus (peace be upon him) that he is one of the servants of God, not as the Christians said of him, that he is the son of God or the third of three; and the declaration that this which has been mentioned is a straight path leading to God and to His Garden.

When Jesus (peace be upon him) came to them with this, the factions, those who formed parties in denial, differed among themselves: each one said of Jesus (peace be upon him) a false saying and rejected what he brought, except those whom God guided among the believers, who bore witness to his messengership, affirmed the truth of all that he brought, and said: he is the servant of God and His messenger. So woe to those who do wrong, that is, how intense is the grief of the wrongdoers!, from the punishment of a painful Day (43:65); and how great is their loss on that Day!

Then We sent following, that is, We caused to follow in their footsteps Our messengers, and We sent following Jesus son of Mary. God singled out Jesus (peace be upon him) because the context concerns the Christians, who claim to follow Jesus. And We gave him the Gospel, which is one of God's excellent books, and We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy, as He, Exalted, said: You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity towards those who believe to be the Jews and those who associate partners with God, and you will surely find the nearest of them in affection towards those who believe to be those who say: We are Christians. That is because among them are priests and monks, and because they are not arrogant (5:82), and the following verses. For this reason the Christians were softer of heart than others when they were upon the law of Jesus (peace be upon him). And monasticism, which they invented: monasticism (rahbāniyya) is worship; they invented of their own accord a form of worship, imposed it upon themselves and bound themselves to its requirements, which God had not written for them nor made obligatory; rather it was they who bound themselves to it of their own accord, their intent in that being the good pleasure of God. Yet despite that, they did not observe it with its due observance, that is, they did not carry it out nor fulfil its rights. So they fell short in two respects: in respect of their innovation, and in respect of their failure to carry out what they had imposed upon themselves. This condition is the predominant one among their conditions, though among them are those who are upright upon the command of God, and for this reason He said: So We gave those of them who believed their reward, that is, those who believed in Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) together with their faith in Jesus: God gave each one according to his faith; but many of them are corrupt (57:27).

He, Exalted, says, informing of the obstinacy of the earlier Children of Israel whom Jesus son of Mary called, saying to them: O Children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of God to you, that is, God has sent me to call you to good and forbid you evil, and He has supported me with manifest proofs. Among what indicates my truthfulness is my being confirming what is before me of the Torah, that is, I have come with what Moses brought of the Torah and the heavenly laws; had I been a false claimant to prophethood, I would have come with other than what the messengers brought. And confirming what is before me of the Torah also in that it told of me and gave glad tidings of me, so I came and was sent confirming it. And bringing glad tidings of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Aḥmad: he is Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, the Hāshimite Prophet. So Jesus (upon him be blessings and peace) is like all the prophets: he confirms the preceding prophet and gives glad tidings of the prophet to come, unlike the liars, who contradict the prophets in the most extreme contradiction and oppose them in attributes, character, command and prohibition. Then when he came to them, Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him), of whom Jesus gave glad tidings, with the clear proofs, that is, the manifest evidences indicating that he is the one, and that he is truly the messenger of God, they said, obstinately resisting the truth and denying it: This is manifest sorcery (61:6). This is among the most astonishing of wonders: the Messenger whose messengership had become clear and more manifest than the sun of the day is made out to be a sorcerer whose sorcery is manifest! Is there any abandonment by God greater than this?! And is there any fabrication more extreme than this fabrication, which denied of him what was known of his messengership and attributed to him what he was the furthest of people from?!
